recent_posts.title: LLMs produce forgeries and it is okay not to use AI
recent_posts.summary: A critical essay arguing that LLMs produce forgeries rather than authentic work, and that the 'inevitability' framing around AI adoption is a manufactured narrative. The author draws parallels between AI-generated code and forgery, arguing that vibe-coding degrades software craft, burdens open source maintainers with low-quality contributions, and creates plausible deniability around intellectual property. The piece contends that real attribution is technically impossible with current LLMs, and that AI output should be treated as a forgery unless proven otherwise. It also notes that video games are one market where consumers have successfully pushed back against unlabeled AI content.

recent_posts.title: Why the DOM needs fundamental redesign for modern web applications
recent_posts.summary: The DOM has become bloated with over 350 properties per node and 660 CSS properties, making it unsuitable for modern web applications. CSS's inside-out layout model creates complexity, while features like flexbox require speculative layout passes that can cause performance issues. The author argues for rethinking web UI from first principles, proposing simpler layout models that separate concerns and provide better primitives for building applications. Current proposals like HTML-in-Canvas are insufficient because they don't address the fundamental architectural problems of the web platform.

recent_posts.title: Occlusion with Bells On
recent_posts.summary: Use.GPU 0.14 introduces significant upgrades including modern SSAO/GTAO implementation, improved render pass infrastructure, and expanded shader generation. The upgraded inspector and the detailed use of temporal accumulation and reprojection in rendering pipelines are highlights. Efforts focus on simplifying GPU API designs while maintaining modularity and flexibility.

recent_posts.title: The Bouquet Residence
recent_posts.summary: In the wake of a significant outage at CrowdStrike, the CEO issued a straightforward announcement focused on facts and relief logistics. A communication professional's alternative statement, though stylistically polished and empathetic, was critiqued for shifting focus from actionable details to personal feelings and promises. The post argues that effective communication in technical crises should prioritize clear, factual information over empathetic expression. It also discusses the broader cultural shift in tech communications towards more inclusive and emotionally driven styles and critiques this shift for its potential to mismanage actual technical crises.

recent_posts.title: Stable Fiddusion
recent_posts.summary: This post explores the design and generation of blue noise in frequency space, and how it can be used in computer graphics. It covers topics such as the definition of blue noise, the difference between blue noise and white noise, and the key properties of blue noise. The post also delves into the mathematical aspects of designing and optimizing blue noise in frequency space.

recent_posts.title: Sub-pixel Distance Transform
recent_posts.summary: The Sub-pixel Distance Transform (ESDT) is a technique for rendering fonts accurately using Signed Distance Fields (SDFs). It provides subpixel accuracy and solves issues with traditional Euclidean Distance Transforms (EDTs). The ESDT algorithm involves calculating subpixel offsets for gray pixels and propagating distances to nearby pixels. It also addresses the problem of blending colors at the edges of glyphs. The ESDT implementation provides high-quality font rendering at different font sizes and scales.

recent_posts.title: Fuck It, We'll Do It Live
recent_posts.summary: This post describes the implementation of the Live effect run-time and the main parts of the Live component model. It explains how Live components work and how they rely on concepts like fibers, hooks, and state. The post also touches on the topics of context, captures, fences, and the use of resources in Live components.

recent_posts.title: Teardown Frame Teardown
recent_posts.summary: Teardown is a game with a voxel-driven engine that allows for a fully destructible environment. The game utilizes raytracing for global illumination, real-time reflections, and physically convincing smoke and fire. It employs a deferred G-buffer for rendering, with separate draw calls for each object in the game. Teardown also incorporates volumetric shadow maps, blue noise sampling, and denoising techniques for lighting and reflections. The post-processing stage includes motion blur, depth of field, temporal anti-aliasing, bloom, and lens distortion effects. Overall, Teardown's rendering techniques create a visually impressive and immersive experience.

recent_posts.title: Use.GPU Goes Trad
recent_posts.summary: Use.GPU is an experimental reactive/declarative WebGPU framework that aims to make GPU rendering easier and more sane. The 0.8 release fills the gaps with conveniences like scenes and nodes with matrices, instancing meshes, shadow maps for lighting, and visibility culling for geometry. It also introduces a data-driven, scriptable render pipeline that combines the benefits of immediate-mode UI with extensibility. Use.GPU's reactivity allows for one-way data flow and consistent resolution of state changes
